title: An Evaluation of the Readability and Content-Quality of Pelvic Organ Prolapse YouTube Transcripts
screen_reason: Content analysis of the first 100 English-narrated YouTube videos returned for 'pelvic organ prolapse'. Beyond readability (the paper's primary outcome, not relevant here), the authors rated misinformation on a 1-5 Likert scale by comparing each transcript's content to accepted POP management recommendations and the IUGA/ICS joint report guidelines, and report the share of transcripts scoring >=3: 'Fifteen percent of video transcripts had highly misinformative content'. That is a share of items judged inaccurate against an external clinical ground truth, with a stated denominator of 100 transcripts, so it is CONTENT. The DISCERN and PEMAT scores are quality/completeness instruments and are coded QUALITY.

estimates.country: Not stated; English-language YouTube search run by a US-based team
estimates.date: Not stated; videos published 2009-2019, manuscript submitted November 2020
estimates.measure_type: % of POP YouTube video transcripts rated as having highly misinformative content (misinformation Likert >=3 of 5, against IUGA/ICS guidelines)
estimates.denominator: 100 English-narrated YouTube video transcripts from the first 135 results for the search term 'pelvic organ prolapse'
estimates.definition: Transcript scored 3 or higher on a 1-5 misinformation Likert scale, rated by comparing its content to accepted POP management recommendations from educational literature and the IUGA/ICS joint report guidelines (example given: describing surgical management before attempting more conservative options)
estimates.misinfo_def: "Misinformation was evaluated using a likert scale (1= no misinformation to 5 = high misinformation) by comparing content to accepted POP management recommendations from educational literature and an International Urogynecological Association (IUGA)/International Continence Society (ICS) joint report guidelines, as the reference measure."
estimates.source_quote: Fifteen percent of video transcripts had highly misinformative content (Likert score ≥3 out of 5, n = 15) (Table 3).
estimates.page_loc: Results, 'Accuracy', p. 122; Table 3 row 'High Misinformation (DISCERN score ≥3)'
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Trained reviewers scored each transcript against accepted POP management recommendations and the IUGA/ICS joint report. Reliability handled by training reviewers on each video and resolving discrepancies to consensus; no kappa or ICC reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: The readability of the ﬁrst 135 YouTube videos were assessed using an unaltered/unsorted search algorithm. Videos were excluded from the study if they were not narrated in English (n = 4), contained neither text or audio (n = 1), demonstrated a surgical procedure (n = 8), or >10 minutes in length (as user engagement declines after 10 minutes)17 (n = 22). After exclusion criteria was applied, 100 videos remained.
estimates.notes: country_norm = Global because the paper states no country restriction on the videos; the search was English-only and the framing is US patient literacy, but no locale is reported. The complementary figure, 'Low Misinformation (DISCERN score <3) 85%', is stated verbatim in the abstract and Table 3 and is the exact complement; only the misinformation-positive share is extracted. The paper labels the misinformation variable 'DISCERN score' in Table 3 but describes it in Methods as a separate 1-5 misinformation Likert; the threshold is also inconsistent (Table 3 'DISCERN score >=3' vs text 'Likert score >=3 out of 5' with the low band defined as <3, which is at least self-consistent).

estimates.date: Not stated; videos published 2009-2019, manuscript submitted November 2020
estimates.measure_type: % of POP YouTube video transcripts rated moderate to poor quality on DISCERN (score <=3 of 5)
estimates.denominator: 100 English-narrated YouTube video transcripts from the first 135 results for the search term 'pelvic organ prolapse'
estimates.definition: DISCERN quality score of 3 or below out of 5 (failure to mention sources of content, unbiased information, different treatment options, and associated risks and benefits)
estimates.misinfo_def: "The DISCERN questionnaire is a widely used instrument that encompasses key components of POP guidelines, including whether the item describes treatment options, beneﬁts, risks, and/or shared decision-making."
estimates.page_loc: Table 3, 'Low Quality Transcripts' block; text version at Results, 'Quality', p. 122
estimates.ground_truth_detail: DISCERN questionnaire applied by trained reviewers; discrepancies resolved to consensus. No reliability statistic reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: We reported nearly three-fourths of transcripts contained poor quality content (ie, failed to mention sources of content, unbiased information, different treatment options, and associated risk and beneﬁts of treatments).
estimates.notes: QUALITY, not prevalence: a wholly accurate transcript can score low on DISCERN simply by omitting treatment options, sources or risk/benefit discussion. Kept for the appendix only.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: PEMAT understandability/actionability shares (48% and 33% high; 52% and 67% low), shared-decision-making shares (23% high, 53% low), 'high quality (DISCERN >3) 29%', '10% of transcripts encompassed all metrics to be considered high quality', '1% completely poor quality', and commercial bias 19%/no commercial bias 81%. All are completeness, usability or bias measures, not veracity, so they add nothing beyond the one QUALITY row already recorded. Content-coverage shares (anatomy complete 30%, causes 56%, symptoms 64%, surgical repair 59%, PFMT 36%, pessary 31%, no treatment 14%) are topic coverage, not accuracy. Readability medians (12.6 overall etc.) are scale scores, not shares of misinformation, so no row. Comment-section counts (medical advice requested 19%, advertising 7%) are unrelated to misinformation prevalence. The 85% 'low misinformation' figure is the exact complement of the extracted 15% and is not entered separately.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis. Frame: unaltered/unsorted YouTube search for 'pelvic organ prolapse' (chosen over 'rectocele' and 'cystocele' for having the most results, 7390); first 135 videos assessed, 35 excluded (4 not narrated in English, 1 with neither text nor audio, 8 surgical procedure demonstrations, 22 longer than 10 minutes), leaving 100. Transcripts downloaded from YouTube and edited for punctuation and spelling; title and description omitted. Instruments: three readability formulas (Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning Fog, SMOG), DISCERN, PEMAT, plus a 1-5 misinformation Likert against IUGA/ICS guidelines. Reliability: reviewers trained on each video and discrepancies discussed to consensus; no quantitative inter-rater statistic reported. Search date not stated. No sampling weights or response rate apply.
